correct_answer: Two failures (SEC-0891 and SEC-0923) — the CISO's Slack message establishes the description of controls as binding, making SEC-0891 non-compliant at 26 days without exception; SEC-1003 had proper exception approval
rationale: The critical signal is the CISO's statement in Slack that the SOC2 description of controls (14-day SLA) is the binding standard, NOT the internal policy version. This means: SEC-0891 (26 days, no exception filed, Priya's Jira comment incorrectly relied on v3.1's 30-day window) is a control failure — the CISO clarified on the same day that the description of controls governs, but no exception was filed retroactively. SEC-0923 (17 days, compensating WAF control noted but NO CISO approval and NO exception ticket) is also a failure — the description of controls requires CISO approval for compensating controls, which was never obtained. SEC-1003 (17 days, proper exception with CISO approval) is compliant — the description of controls explicitly allows extended timelines with CISO approval. Answer A incorrectly applies the internal policy version instead of the description of controls, ignoring the CISO's definitive Slack statement. Answer D misses that the CISO's Slack clarification retroactively establishes SEC-0891 as non-compliant (Priya relied on the wrong standard). Answer D incorrectly treats SEC-1003 as a failure despite having the exact exception process the control description allows.
